_comment: Felling — the gob, the fall and what it scores. docs/01-gdd/06-felling-system.md is the spec; these are its numbers.
_archComment: Brickwork arches over the hole you cut, which is the only reason a 40 kN prop is any use under a 9400 kN chimney: a prop carries the wall directly above it up to the height the arch forms, about five metres of it, and the rest goes round the opening to the crescent. At Waterside that is 22 kN on a good prop - one hole next door takes it to 33 and it stands, two takes it to 44 and it splits. Which is why the loop is cut two cells, set a prop, cut two cells.
_shiftComment: What a felling costs in daylight. The 40 seconds a metre is the design's own number and the reason Act 2 is a decision rather than a chore: accuracy is bought with daylight and there is no other currency for it. Cutting and propping are priced so that a worked gob - 56 cells and 14 props - is about half a shift, which leaves the other half to argue over.
